messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

Those NCEs seem reasonable to me. I’d add clear access to the pad and keeping the trailer out of the way, while avoiding damage and unnecessary noise. I’m not sure about storing it here longer term, and I’d rather not be asked to choose between you. I haven’t asked my landlord, so I can’t agree to a change in the pad arrangement yet. I have no hard dates to offer in the next few weeks; daytime pickup with advance notice seems preferable, but we’d need to agree on a date and return plan.

I can’t give exact dates or times yet, but I need the trailer within the next few weeks to haul materials for my home project. The timing can shift somewhat; it can’t just wait until A is finished. A and I work together, but that doesn’t affect my use or timing.

My NCEs are getting a fair share of use, timely access, safe use, clear pickup and return times, and flexibility if plans change. B’s list sounds reasonable; I can give advance notice, use daytime pickup, avoid damage and noise, keep the trailer out of the way, and return it as agreed. For an overlap, let’s agree on separate use blocks soon rather than ask B to choose sides.

I don’t disagree with your NCEs. Mine are freedom to use the trailer, timely access for my trips, and clear, fair arrangements for pickup, return, and care.

I don’t have exact dates or times to give yet. I want it for weekend trips in the next few weeks; there’s no firmer deadline, and I may be able to shift which weekend. I’d need it for a weekend, but haven’t set pickup or return times. C being my coworker doesn’t affect my use or timing.

If dates overlap, a fair fallback could be alternating weekends or choosing dates by mutual agreement. I don’t know whether B’s pad affects pickup or return; I’d want the trailer returned safely and in good condition.

That list is right. I can’t yet name the earliest pickup date or block length; I need to confirm when the materials and project are ready. I’ll give advance notice as soon as I have that schedule. One block each before anyone gets a second fits my NCEs.

I don’t disagree with your added NCEs. One block each before a second seems fair. I’m less sure about the overlap rule; I’d rather the two users work it out without putting me in the middle, and I can’t choose between you. Two days’ notice and daytime pickup and return should work, subject to access and landlord approval. I haven’t asked my landlord yet, so I can’t give a report-back date. I’d need it returned in good condition and parked out of the way. The landlord’s rules and whether the pad is accessible are the main things that could limit dates.

I agree with one block each before anyone gets a second. I don’t accept item four as written: “more date-bound” shouldn’t be decided until we compare the actual constraints. My project needs to happen within the next few weeks, even though I can’t set dates until the materials are ready.

I can’t name open dates, block length, or a confirmation date yet. Two days’ notice seems workable once I have the materials schedule, but I can’t promise it before then. I know of no other limits on my use; pad access and landlord approval still need checking. I agree with your added NCEs.

I don’t disagree with your added NCEs. One block each before anyone gets a second seems fair. I can accept the overlap rule if the next open block for the flexible user is agreed promptly, not left open-ended.

I haven’t chosen specific weekends yet; I’m looking for a weekend in the next few weeks and can shift it. Two days’ notice is enough. I can give firm pickup and return times once we choose a weekend. I don’t know of any limits from the pad, landlord, trailer condition, keys, or paperwork, but I can’t confirm those details.

The revised overlap wording seems fair, especially that I’m not asked to choose. I can ask my landlord and let you both know when I get an answer, though I can’t promise when that will be. Before pickup, please record firm times, who’s collecting it, and confirm pad access. At return, note its condition, any damage, and that it’s parked out of the way; please also return the keys. A and C could check the trailer, keys, and paperwork together before any firm booking, and I can check whether the pad is accessible once we know the landlord’s answer.

I accept the revised overlap wording, including agreeing the next block promptly, and the booking-record details. I can do a joint check with A before any firm booking; I can’t give a date yet, and I’ll update the group once I have the materials schedule.

If the materials and landlord answer don’t arrive in time, I’ll need to find another way to haul for my project rather than wait indefinitely for the trailer.

I accept the revised overlap wording. I don’t have firm weekends yet; I can shift weekends, and I’ll name firm dates once C has the materials schedule and we’ve checked access. Two days’ notice, daytime pickup and return, a shared booking record, and returning the trailer in good condition and out of the way all work for me. I know of no other limits, but I can’t confirm the pad, landlord rules, keys, or paperwork.

I agree with your added NCEs and the final overlap wording. Yes, A and I can set the next block in that same conversation. I’ll agree to a review date and decide on another hauling option if access or the landlord answer is delayed; I can’t name that date yet. I can’t schedule the joint check until I know when the materials schedule is available.

I accept the final overlap wording and B’s booking details. C’s fallback works for me. I’ll do the joint trailer, keys, and paperwork check with C before the first firm booking.

“Agreed promptly” should mean setting the next block in that same conversation; if we can’t agree, pause only the disputed block and keep non-overlapping blocks. I have no specific weekends to offer yet, but I’ll share candidates once C has the materials schedule and we know pad access. If the landlord answer or pad check delays my weekend, I’ll look for another date rather than make a firm booking without confirmed access.

I don’t disagree with the draft or list, except “daytime use”: I agreed to daytime pickup and return, not necessarily daytime use. I can’t name a calendar date for review until I know the materials schedule; I agree it must be set and not left open-ended.

The corrected NCE list looks right to me, and I agree with most of the draft. I can’t agree that I’m kept out of the middle while item five asks me to compare A and C’s needs; if you can’t agree, please pause just the disputed block or use another neutral process. I’m willing to ask my landlord and report the answer, but the trailer staying on the pad is only the current situation, not an arrangement I can promise will continue. Include insurance and registration papers in A and C’s check if applicable; I can’t determine the legal requirements.
